name: Snoqualmie
seo_title: 5 Christmas Events for Kids in Snoqualmie, WA 2026
seo_desc: 5 Christmas events for kids in Snoqualmie, WA, 2 free: Annual Holiday Tree Lighting at Salish Lodge and Spa and more.
lede: Snoqualmie does Christmas in its historic downtown beside the railroad tracks: a tree lighting with Santa's arrival at Railroad Park, Santa mornings at Salish Lodge and holiday trains from the Northwest Railway Museum.
celebrates: Snoqualmie's season starts at Snoqualmie Winter Lights in Railroad Park in Historic Downtown, held on the first Saturday of December. Santa arrives to help count down the tree lighting, and the city says snow is guaranteed during the lighting. School choirs, jazz bands, the Mount Si Carolers and a dance team perform on the main stage. Families drop letters to Santa in a mailbox and take photos in the gazebo beside a holiday tree decorated by a downtown gift shop. A few days later Santa visits Mini Treehouse downtown, and Salish Lodge and Spa lights its own tree and hosts Santa in its restaurant.
lastyear: The City of Snoqualmie held Snoqualmie Winter Lights on Saturday, December 6, 2025, in Historic Downtown Snoqualmie. The city posted photo albums of the Tree Lighting and Santa Arrival on its Flickr page afterward and shared a video of the evening on Facebook, calling it a lovely night that kicked off the holiday season and asking families to save the date for the next year's event on December 5, 2026.
facts: Snoqualmie sits about 30 miles east of Seattle on the river just above Snoqualmie Falls, a 276 foot waterfall that the Snoqualmie Tribe considers a place of powerful magic for peace. Railroad service reached the upper valley in 1889, and the first train was an excursion train, a sign of how early the area drew visitors. Snoqualmie incorporated as a town on June 9, 1903, after 429 residents counted in 1900. Hop farming boomed in the 1880s, and lumber mills lasted long after aphids wiped out the hop crops.
trains: Trains made Snoqualmie. Railroad service reached the upper valley in 1889, and today the Northwest Railway Museum keeps that history alive at the Snoqualmie depot with historic trains that run through the valley, including holiday rides in December. The valley has no Sounder commuter train, Link light rail or Amtrak stop of its own. The nearest hub for Amtrak and Sounder is King Street Station in Seattle, roughly 30 miles west. Seattle also has the Seattle Center Monorail, a short ride on trains from 1961.

traditions: A downtown tree lighting at Railroad Park with Santa's arrival, live music from local school groups and a gazebo for photos.
Children drop off letters to Santa in a mailbox at Railroad Park during Winter Lights.
Santa visits a downtown Snoqualmie shop on a Sunday in mid December, with a quiet first half hour for special needs families.
The lodge above the falls lights its holiday tree on an evening in late November.
Santa visits the lodge restaurant on four Sunday mornings from late November to just before Christmas.

kidfact: Snoqualmie Falls is 276 feet tall, and Santa's tree lighting happens just a short drive away.
faq: In Snoqualmie the city hosts Snoqualmie Winter Lights in Railroad Park, with Santa's arrival, a tree lighting, live music from school groups, face painting, cookie decorating and a letters to Santa mailbox. Salish Lodge adds its own tree lighting and Santa mornings, and the Northwest Railway Museum runs holiday trains.
Where is the Snoqualmie tree lighting held?

The city's tree lighting is at Railroad Park, 7971 Railroad Avenue SE, in Historic Downtown Snoqualmie. The park has a main stage for live music and a gazebo where families take photos with the holiday tree, and it sits among the shops and the depot along Railroad Avenue.
Can kids ride a Christmas train near Snoqualmie?

Yes. The Northwest Railway Museum, based at the Snoqualmie depot, runs holiday train rides in the valley. Check its Santa Trains page for current dates, times and prices before you plan a trip, because the museum sets them and Rally does not sell tickets. The depot sits in Historic Downtown, close to Railroad Park and the other holiday stops.
Is there a quieter way to see Santa in Snoqualmie?

The city lists a Santa visit at Mini Treehouse in downtown Snoqualmie with the first 30 minutes reserved for special needs families. Salish Lodge also offers Santa visits on Sunday mornings in its restaurant, which suits families who prefer a smaller setting and a seated visit. Ask the lodge about booking and prices before you go, because the lodge sets them.
What else is nearby for families in the Snoqualmie Valley?

North Bend has its Holly Days festival and Carnation hosts Christmas in Carnation, both on the first Saturday of December, so families often visit more than one valley community that weekend. Carnation Farms and Remlinger Farms add events on other December days, which gives the whole valley a full holiday calendar for kids.

intro_html:
Rally the corgi has sniffed out the best Christmas events for kids in Snoqualmie for 2026, and here is what he found: 5 family events, 2 of them free. The magic runs from November 29 (Annual Holiday Tree Lighting at Salish Lodge and Spa) through December 20, with Annual Holiday Tree Lighting at Salish Lodge and Spa (November 29), Santa Visits The Restaurant at Salish Lodge and Spa (from November 29) and Yuletide Express at Northwest Railway Museum (from December 4) along the way. We check every date on the host’s own website or an official city calendar, and each listing links straight there. For the rest of the state, see our Washington Christmas events for kids guide.

Planning a bigger day out? Snoqualmie families also use our guide to Christmas events for kids in Seattle, which covers Seattle Center Winterfest, WildLanterns, the North Pole Limited Santa train and more.
